facts.text: Teen Witch began as a female Teen Wolf. It even borrowed that 1985 hit's title lettering and tagline before being reworked into its own story.
Richie Miller is played by Joshua John Miller, son of The Exorcist actor Jason Miller and half-brother of The Lost Boys star Jason Patric.
Dad Frank Miller is Dick Sargent, the second Darrin on the witchy sitcom Bewitched. He'd also played father to another witch daughter, Tabitha, on that show.
Variety called the comedy limited but praised the film's "bouncy score" by Larry and Tom Weir, the songwriting brothers behind every tune you hear.
Teen Witch made just $3,875 in its opening weekend and $27,843 in its whole theatrical run, against a $2.5 million budget. Cable and video made it a cult hit.
An early cut screened at the American Film Market. Producer Paul Mason says the "I Like Boys" cheer got applause there, and the buyers' reaction led to more music being added.
Pop star Debbie Gibson was the first choice to play Louise. Negotiations fell through, and Robyn Lively, then 15, got the part.
Dan Gauthier (Brad) and Lisa Fuller (Randa) met on this set and married in 1990. They're still together, with a son.
Director Dorian Walker wanted comedian Ellen DeGeneres for a teacher role after seeing her in clubs, but studio exec Moshe Diamant vetoed it.
Robyn Lively was 16 when she filmed Teen Witch, while Dan Gauthier, playing high school senior Brad Powell, was 25.
To fit in the songs, producer Alana Lambros tore about 15 pages out of the script and replaced them with blanks reading "Musical Number."
Madame Serena's creepy Victorian house is the same Los Angeles house used in Michael Jackson's Thriller video.
Serena's "Punky Brewster face" line is a wink: star Robyn Lively played Lisa in two episodes of the sitcom Punky Brewster.
Serena's interior was a soundstage with no steps, so Robyn Lively had to crouch down as she walked away to fake descending the exterior stairs.
Polly's "birthday on Elm Street" and "revenge of the cheerleaders" lines nod to A Nightmare on Elm Street (1984) and Revenge of the Cheerleaders (1976).
The first script draft was raunchier, closer to a Porky's-style sex comedy. Producer Alana Lambros and director Dorian Walker cut it down to PG-13.
Robyn Lively says her mother created Louise's 1980s look, and many of the clothes on screen were Lively's own.
The school scenes were shot at Herbert Hoover High in Glendale over winter break, with real students as extras.
Producer Alana Lambros says extras drifted away during the long dance shoot. She let them go, betting viewers would watch the leads.
Caren Kaye (Louise's mom, Margaret) and Joshua John Miller (Richie) also played mother and son on a 1987 episode of 21 Jump Street.
Joshua John Miller, who plays dog-turned-brother Richie, admits "it was a very campy performance" but says he's grown to honor the film.
The podcast How Did This Get Made? devoted episode 130 to Teen Witch. The hosts are avowed fans who single out Richie actor Joshua John Miller's performance.
Producer Alana Lambros says studio boss Moshe Diamant gave her about $1.25 million and a 25-day shoot. Wikipedia lists the budget as $2.5 million.
Director Dorian Walker hired Robert Banas, a dancer in West Side Story, to choreograph the film's dance numbers.
No soundtrack album was released because the backers never funded one. Many songs were sung by members of the songwriting Weir family to save money.
Joshua John Miller says he learned to appreciate the film after drag queen Peaches Christ hosted midnight screenings in San Francisco.
Fans have long wondered why Louise carries birth control pills in her purse when she can't even get a date.
Brad actor Dan Gauthier later played Kevin Buchanan on the soap One Life to Live and Matt Liston on the sitcom Ellen.
"Top That" wasn't in the original script. It was added in reshoots after an early screening, and Mandy Ingber (Polly) says she had an attitude problem on set.
Watch the lips: the audio and video of this rap are slightly out of sync, the most noticeable case among the film's musical numbers.
Songwriter Larry Weir says execs asked him for a rap for the reshoots. He performed it for eight executives who looked unimpressed, then said "I like it."
Mandy Ingber (Polly) has called the film one of her worst summer jobs, saying the rap haunts her. She calls it the best of the worst.
Polly actor Mandy Ingber became a yoga instructor and best-selling author whose clients include Jennifer Aniston and Brooke Shields.
"Never Gonna Be the Same Again" has two singers: Lori Ruso on the opening-sequence version and Cindy Valentine on the concert version.
Songwriter Larry Weir reportedly wrote "Popular Girl" during his first meeting with producer Alana Lambros.
Robyn Lively blames a twisted ankle for her modest dancing in the "most popular girl" number.
The abandoned-house love scene was also added in reshoots, after the American Film Market screening, at studio boss Moshe Diamant's order for a bigger picture.
Robyn Lively has said she's now mortified by her make-out scene with Dan Gauthier.
Robyn Lively said a scene where she and Zelda Rubinstein (Madame Serena) share a lap was shot after lunch, and Rubinstein's bad breath made keeping a straight face hard.
In the Philippines, the film reportedly topped ratings after a local release swapped in music from Michael Jackson's Thriller album, producer Alana Lambros says.
Robyn Lively's first two movies, The Best of Times and Wildcats, were both about high school football, and she played the daughter of Robin Williams and Goldie Hawn.
In 2008 Variety reported Ashley Tisdale would star in a Teen Witch remake. It never happened.
The Austin Chronicle's Ada Calhoun called it "a masterpiece of both the teen and witch genres" and "so Eighties it hurts."
The red-zipper-shirt guy and gray-outfit girl in this dance also danced in the earlier harvest dance. The same decorations are visible.
When her sister Blake Lively married Ryan Reynolds in 2012, Robyn Lively performed this "Finest Hour" dance at the wedding and gave Blake the film's necklace.
The Los Angeles improv troupe The Groundlings staged a live comedy musical of Teen Witch in 2013 and 2017.
Chris Willman of the Los Angeles Times panned the film, mentioning its "horrifying pop songs, French kissing, blatant product plugs and Dick Sargent (formerly of Bewitched)."
Huffington Post's Stephanie Marcus called "Top That" the worst song of all time. It has been parodied, including by Alia Shawkat.
